recipes.name: Campbell's Easy Chicken and Cheese Enchiladas
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Chicken Soup (Regular, 98% Fat Free or Healthy Request®)

steps.text: Stir soup, sour cream, picante sauce, and chili powder in a medium bowl until combined.
Transfer 1 cup of the soup-sauce mixture into a large bowl; stir in chicken and cheese.

Divide chicken mixture among the tortillas. Roll up the tortillas and place them seam side up in 11x8-inch shallow baking dish. Pour the remaining picante sauce mixture over the filled tortillas. Cover the baking dish.
Bake at 350 degrees F until the enchiladas are hot and bubbling, about 40 minutes. Top with tomato and onion.

raw_recipe.headline: Campbell's Easy Chicken and Cheese Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: A creamy filling of chicken, sour cream, and cheese gets an added "kick" stirred into it with Pace Picante Sauce. Rolled up in tortillas and baked until bubbly, these enchiladas couldn't be easier, or any more delicious.

review.reviewBody: When rolling enchiladas ( which I have been doing for about 50 years) always heat the tortillas before adding filling and rolling. If they are still diffacult dip in some hot liquid or oil . After rolling place SEAM SIDE DOWN. Love to all and good eating Jerri

This recipe is a really great base for the enchiladas. I doctor mine up a little bit though. I make my chicken in the crockpot. I put my chicken breaks in the crockpot with some black bean and corn salsa and chili powder and let that cook all day. By dinner time the chicken just falls apart. I then mix that chicken in with the soup mix that the recipe calls for. I mix everything and bake as directed but the last 15 minutes I pull the foil off and top with cheese. It comes out all ooey and gooey and bubbly and delicious!

Few changes :). I doubled it and used one can of healthy request cream of cheddar and one of chicken. I also used low-fat sour cream and put in a packet of taco seasoning for the spices. I sprayed the pan and put some Mexican rice under the enchiladas. Covered the top with low-fat Mexican cheese. So good!
I put the chicken and cheese in the sauce. Then I wrap it like a chimichanga. Then I bake till golden. Then I add cheese for the last 10 to 15 mins. Served with sour cream and baby spinach.

I have made this numerous times and each time experimenting with a different addition. (Ortega roasted chilies, sliced black olives, beans, etc.) This is a wonderful recipe for QUICK cravings of enchiladas. Made as-is, it's a little blah but good. Heat the tortillas to help with wrapping and use corn, not flour. **Update, May 2018 - I strongly recommend seam side down or you will have a floppy mess on your hands. I've also done this by layering like a lasagna, too...less work.
Very good. I replaced picante sauce with green chile sauce and used corn tortillas. I layered like a lasagna instead of rolling them.

Love this! It was delicious! Prep time was longer than 10 mins for me but still worth it. So yummy! I’ve already made them twice! The second time I made them, I already had the chicken prepared, had seasoned it, cooked it and cut it up, then froze it to save time. Put it in the fridge a couple days before, and saved so much time! Less prep after a long day at work.

This is a family favorite for sure! The only changes other than using 2 store bought rotisserie chicken breasts per each 6 person serving, was that in the directions, as I just made a quadruple batch, it doesn't multiply the amount of sour cream, soup, picante and chili powder mixture added to the chicken and cheese. You should add one extra cup of of the soup mixture per each 6 person serving. I could literally make this with my eyes shut. I also omit the green onions and tomatoes as the enchiladas themselves have enough flavor and density. Also, after spraying each pan with non stick cooking spray, I also spread a little of the soup mixture into the bottom of the pan. The final results are amazing and it's even better as leftovers the next day!

I absolutely LOVE this recipe. I have always made it exactly as described. However recently I have been looking for ways to lower my carb intake and instead of tortillas I used zucchini boats. I actually liked them better this way believe it or not. I halved a few zucchinis and hollowed out the middle. Heavily salted both sides and let sit for 15 minutes (key to ensure the enchiladas don’t come out too watery) then rinsed and patted dry before filling with enchilada mix. Bake as usual.
Loved it! Substituted Salsa Verde for the sauce. Used taco seasoning for the chile powder. Next time I’ll add a can of diced green chilies to the mix.

This was delicious! I added a 4oz can of diced green chiles to the soup mix and used 2 tsp of taco seasoning (instead of chili powder) and followed the rest of the recipe as is, though it did fill more than 6 tortillas, so you may want to have a few extra on hand. So tasty! Will definitely make again!
I make this with keto wraps for a delicious meal I can eat.
Super easy! I used an entire rotisserie chicken and added 1/2 can of Rotel mild diced tomatoes and cilantro to the mixture for extra flavor and used a little extra picante sauce. Family loved it!
Easy to make and taste great.
These were easy to make and quite tasty. When hubby goes back for seconds, I know I made a really good dish.
This was delish! Could have used black olives, maybe next time. I also could have cooked it a little longer to crisp it more, but it was still very good.
Love this recipe. Last time I used mild cheddar cheese. They were still really good.
Family loved it
It was very good. It just needs a little..punch to it. Maybe taco sauce?
I make this all the time. My family loves it. I do use a little more chili powder and also shred the chicken as well. It's a hit with all my family and friends.
